label: Earthfast Timber Posts (in Ground)
volunteer_identification_guide: Round bush logs or split posts sunk directly into post-holes without pads; highly susceptible to termite attack and rot at ground-line; diagnostic of rapid/vernacular pioneer construction.

label: Round Timber Stumps / Blocks
volunteer_identification_guide: Hardwood tree rounds set on flat bedplates or stone pads, terminating 200-600mm above ground level; may have tin ant-caps (post-1880s).

label: Horizontal Timber Bedlogs on Ground
volunteer_identification_guide: Large unsquared tree trunks laid flat on cleared surface acting as direct ground sills; common in outstations, barns, and woolshed sweat pens.

label: Dry-stone Piers / Rubble Footing
volunteer_identification_guide: Unmortared local fieldstone stacked as dwarf piers or continuous perimeter dwarf wall; stones wedged with spalls.

label: Mortared Stone Foundation Wall
volunteer_identification_guide: Continuous perimeter wall of dressed or rubblestone bonded with soft sand-lime or clay mortar; provides solid base for masonry or timber superstructures.

label: Brick Piers (Isolated)
volunteer_identification_guide: Square masonry pillars (typically 230x230mm / 9x9 inch) supporting floor bearers at 1.5-2.0m spacing; allows sub-floor cross-ventilation.

label: Concrete Piers / Continuous Slab
volunteer_identification_guide: Mass concrete piers (with blue metal aggregate, post-1890s) or unreinforced/reinforced ground slab (post-1900); modern replacement or 20th-century sheds.

label: Steel Posts / Rail Track Uprights
volunteer_identification_guide: Galvanised iron pipe or recycled railway track rails used as sturdy fireproof/termite-proof piers.

label: Round Bush Poles (Unfinished)
volunteer_identification_guide: Unhewn logs with bark removed or partially intact; rough rustic framing using locally felled trees (box, ironbark, stringybark).

label: Adzed / Broadaxe Squared Timber
volunteer_identification_guide: Logs squared with broadaxe or adze; leaves distinctive scallop-shaped gouges and undulating surfaces along the facets.

label: Pit-sawn Timber (Manual)
volunteer_identification_guide: Cut with two-man hand pit-saw; reveals characteristic irregular, slightly diagonal, criss-cross saw marks with varied spacing between strokes.

label: Circular-sawn Timber (Steam Mill)
volunteer_identification_guide: Cut in commercial steam sawmills; leaves regular, curved concentric arc marks across the face of the timber; widespread after mid-1850s.

label: Band-sawn / Modern Planed Milled
volunteer_identification_guide: Modern dimensional lumber; fine straight parallel lines perpendicular to grain or perfectly smooth planed surface with standardized metric/imperial dimensions.

label: High Potential - Intact Underfloor Accumulation
volunteer_identification_guide: Undisturbed deep void beneath intact timber floorboards; accumulative trap for dropped coins, buttons, pins, paper, tobacco tins, bone, and swept detritus.

label: Moderate Potential - Partial Floor Loss / Slats
volunteer_identification_guide: Sub-floor space partially exposed, disturbed by vermin or livestock, or woolshed dung accumulation with scattered dropped artefacts.

label: Low Potential - Cleared / Stock Disturbed
volunteer_identification_guide: Shallow crawlspace that has been flushed out, eroded, or heavily disturbed by burrowing animals or scavengers.

label: None - Earthen Floor or Solid Ground Slab
volunteer_identification_guide: Floor sits directly on earth or solid concrete; zero underfloor void exists, though buried occupation layers may exist underneath.
